title: Malay Annals (Malacca-Iskandar Bridge), Pseudo-Methodius, Bochart, Isidore, Africanus, Paschale, Gregory of Tours, Lombards, Iceland, Wales, Keating Ireland, Tarikh-i-Rashidi, Ladakh, Rajasthan, Harivamsha, Matsya Purana, Classical Greece/Rome, Kojiki & Korea

nodes.name: Raja Secander / Iskandar Zulkarnain + Princess Shaher-ul Beriah (dau. of Raja Kida Hindi)
nodes.era: 4th c. BCE → Legendary Malay Origin (Sejarah Melayu Ch. 1)
nodes.role: Malay Annals Royal Bridge to Alexander the Great (Two-Horned)
sources: Sejarah Melayu / Malay Annals (John Leyden 1821 pp.3–10)
nodes.notes: Chapter 1 of the Malay Annals (Sejarah Melayu / Sulalat al-Salatin) records the marriage of Raja Secander (Iskandar Zulkarnain / Alexander the Great) to Princess Shaher-ul Beriah, daughter of defeated Indian King Raja Kida Hindi, birthing the ancestral Malay dynasty.

nodes.name: Raja Aristun Shah → Raja Aftus → Raja Suran (Conqueror of Gangga Nagara & Chola Link)
nodes.era: Legendary / Early Malay-Indian Horizon (Sejarah Melayu Ch. 1–2)
nodes.role: Ancestral Malay-Chola Sovereign Bridging India & Malay Peninsula
sources: Sejarah Melayu / Malay Annals (John Leyden 1821 pp.10–24)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Raja Secander via Aristun Shah -> Aftus -> Raja Shulan; campaigned across Perak (Gangga Nagara) and married Princess Onang Kiu before descending to the sea-kingdom and fathering three royal brothers.

nodes.name: Sang Sapurba / Sri Tri Buana (Bukit Seguntang, Palembang / Srivijaya)
nodes.role: Srivijaya-Palembang Progenitor Appearing on Mt. Siguntang
sources: Sejarah Melayu / Malay Annals Ch. 2–3
nodes.notes: Son of Raja Suran and descended from Raja Secander; appeared on Bukit Seguntang (Palembang, Sumatra), wed Wan Sendari daughter of Demang Lebar Daun, and inaugurated the Malay Sriwijaya royal covenant.

nodes.name: Sang Nila Utama (Founder of Kingdom of Singapura, 1299 CE)
nodes.role: Founder & First Raja of Ancient Singapore (Singapura)
sources: Sejarah Melayu / Malay Annals Ch. 3–6
nodes.notes: Son of Sang Sapurba who sighted a lion-beast at Temasek, named it Singapura ('Lion City'), and founded the five-king Singapura royal line leading to Iskandar Shah.

nodes.name: Parameswara / Sultan Iskandar Shah (Founder of Malacca Sultanate, 1400 CE — Bridged via Malay Annals!)
nodes.role: Last King of Singapura & Founder of the Malacca Sultanate
sources: Sejarah Melayu / Malay Annals Ch. 10–11
Ming Shi-lu
nodes.notes: Formerly Pending Bridge in v16.0: graduated into Biblically Connected via Sejarah Melayu's explicit continuous descent from Sang Nila Utama -> Sang Sapurba -> Raja Suran -> Raja Aristun Shah -> Raja Secander (Iskandar Zulkarnain)!

nodes.name: Sultan Mansur Shah (1459–1477) → Sultan Mahmud Shah (1488–1511) → Johor-Riau Sultans
nodes.role: Golden Age & Continuity of the Malacca-Johor Dynasty
sources: Sejarah Melayu / Malay Annals Ch. 14–34
nodes.notes: Sultan Mansur Shah (+ Princess Hang Li Po of Ming China & Princess Raden Galoh of Majapahit) expanded Malacca across the Malay Peninsula & Sumatra; son Sultan Mahmud Shah established the successor Johor Sultanate.

nodes.name: King Phol of Ethiopia → Princess Chouseth / Chuseth (+ Philip II → Alexander; + Byzas → Byzantia)
nodes.role: Ethiopic-Macedonian Maternal Bridge in Pseudo-Methodius
sources: Apocalypse of Pseudo-Methodius (Garstad DOML 14, 2012 pp.25–33, 69–71, 137)
nodes.notes: Pseudo-Methodius identifies Alexander the Great's mother as Ethiopian princess Chouseth/Chuseth (daughter of King Phol of Ethiopia/Cush!), who later married Byzas, founder of Byzantium!

nodes.name: Byzas (Byzantium) → Byzantia (+ Romulus Armelaus) → Armelaus (Rome), Urbanus (Byzantium) & Claudius (Alexandria)
nodes.role: Ethiopian-Greek-Roman Imperial Genealogical Charter
sources: Apocalypse of Pseudo-Methodius Ch. 9 (Garstad DOML 14 pp.27–33, 69–71)
nodes.notes: In Pseudo-Methodius Ch. 9, Chouseth & Byzas bear daughter Byzantia, who marries Roman king Romulus Armelaus (receiving Rome as dowry!) and bears three sons dividing Rome, Byzantium, and Alexandria.

nodes.name: Jonitus / Yonton in Hiliu Chara ('Country of the Sun') & City of Jonetos (Pseudo-Methodius Ch. 3)
nodes.role: 4th Son of Noah's Eastern Astronomer Kingdom
sources: Apocalypse of Pseudo-Methodius Ch. 3 (Garstad DOML 14 pp.17, 125)
nodes.notes: Preserves the Latin/Greek recension of Yonton: Noah's post-Flood son Jonitus enters Hiliu Chara ('Country of the Sun' in the East), receives wisdom & astronomy from God, and instructs Nimrod.

nodes.name: Samuel Bochart's Phaleg & Canaan (1712): Exhaustive Table of Nations & Phoenician Colonies
nodes.era: 1646 / 1712 Opera Omnia (Geographia Sacra: Phaleg et Chanaan)
nodes.role: Foundational Comparative Philology of Genesis 10
sources: Samuel Bochart Opera Omnia: Phaleg & Canaan (Lugduni Batavorum 1712)
nodes.notes: Monumental 770-page Latin treatise mapping Peleg's dispersion (Phaleg) and Canaanite-Phoenician maritime colonies (Chanaan) across Africa, Hispania/Tartessos, Gaul, and Britain.

nodes.name: Isidore of Seville's Etymologies Book IX.ii (c. 630 CE): Goths from Magog, Spaniards from Tubal, Gauls from Gomer & Saracens from Ishmael
nodes.role: Most Influential Early Medieval European Ethnographic Key
sources: Isidore of Seville The Etymologies Book IX.ii (Barney et al. 2006 pp.192–200)
nodes.notes: Systematizes the 72 post-Babel nations: 15 from Japheth (Gomer -> Galatians/Gauls; Magog -> Scythians/Goths; Tubal -> Iberians/Spaniards), 30 from Ham, and 27 from Shem.

nodes.name: Julius Africanus's Chronographia & Epistle to Aristides (c. 221 CE): Ogyges, Inachus, Moses & Matthew/Luke Levirate Key
nodes.role: Pioneer Christian World Chronography & Gospel Genealogy Harmonization
sources: Julius Africanus Extant Writings (Ante-Nicene Fathers Vol. VI pp.125–140)
nodes.notes: Synchronizes Ogyges & Inachus with Moses (Exodus 1020 yrs before 1st Olympiad) and preserves the earliest Christian family-tradition reconciliation of Matthew 1 & Luke 3 via Levirate marriage between Matthan and Melchi's houses!

nodes.name: Chronicon Paschale (284–628 CE) & John Malalas Chronographia: Diamerismos & Anastasius → Justin I → Justinian I
nodes.role: Byzantine Universal Chronicles from Adam & Table of Nations to 628 CE
sources: Chronicon Paschale (Whitby 1989; Dindorf 1832)
John Malalas Chronographia Books 8–18 (Downey 1940; Jeffreys 1986)
nodes.notes: Includes the ancient Hippolytan Diamerismos of Earth among Noah's sons and full imperial annals of Zeno, Anastasius, Justin I, Justinian I, Maurice, and Heraclius.

nodes.name: A.H. Sayce (Races of the Old Testament, 1891) & George Rawlinson (Origin of Nations, 1883): Genesis 10 Ethnology
nodes.role: 19th-Century Assyriological & Egyptological Table of Nations Studies
sources: A.H. Sayce The Races of the Old Testament (1891)
George Rawlinson The Origin of Nations (1883)
nodes.notes: Maps biblical Table of Nations ethnonyms onto cuneiform and Egyptian monument inscriptions (Gimirrai = Gomer, Ashkuza = Ashkenaz, Madai = Medes, Muski = Meshech, Khatti = Heth).

nodes.name: Gregory of Tours's Merovingian Dynasty: Childeric I (+ Basina) → Clovis I (+ St. Clotilde) → Chlothar I → Sigibert I (+ Brunhild) & Chilperic I (+ Fredegund)
nodes.era: 457–639 CE (Gregory of Tours History of the Franks)
nodes.role: Primary Chronicle of the Christianized Frankish Kings & Queens
sources: Gregory of Tours History of the Franks (Brehaut 1916 Books I–X)
nodes.notes: Follows Book I Creation-to-Gaul summary into Merovingian royal family politics: Clovis I's baptism under Burgundian Queen Clotilde, sons Theuderic, Chlodomer, Childebert I, Chlothar I, and the fateful rivalry of Queens Brunhild and Fredegund.

nodes.name: Matriarch Gambara → Ibor & Aio → King Agelmund (Origins of the Lombards / Langobards from Scandinavia)
nodes.era: c. 4th–5th c. CE (Paul the Deacon Book I)
nodes.role: Founding Matriarch & Leaders of the Winnili / Lombards
sources: Paul the Deacon History of the Langobards (Foulke 1906 Book I)
nodes.notes: Records the migration of the Winnili (later Langobards) from Scadinavia under mother-counselor Gambara and sons Ibor and Aio, crowning Agelmund son of Aio as first Lombard king.

nodes.name: King Audoin → King Alboin (Conqueror of Italy, 568 CE) → King Authari (+ Queen Theodelinda)
nodes.role: Founders of the Lombard Kingdom of Italy
sources: Paul the Deacon History of the Langobards Books I–IV
nodes.notes: Alboin led the Lombards into Northern Italy (Lombardy, 568 CE); Bavarian princess Queen Theodelinda (correspondent of Pope Gregory I) bridged the Catholic orthodoxy under Authari & Agilulf.

nodes.name: King Rothari (Edict of 643) → King Liutprand (712–744) → King Desiderius (756–774 CE)
nodes.role: Golden Age & Charlemagne Bridge of Lombard Italy
sources: Paul the Deacon History of the Langobards Books IV–VI
nodes.notes: Rothari codified the Edictum Rothari; Liutprand brought Lombard Italy to its height; Desiderius wed his daughter Desiderata to Charlemagne before Pavia fell in 774.

nodes.name: Ingolfur Arnarson (1st Permanent Settler of Iceland, Reykjavik 874 CE) & Foster-Brother Hjorleifur
nodes.role: Norwegian Founding Patriarch of Iceland
sources: Ari Thorgilsson / Ellwood Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok 1898)
nodes.notes: Descended from Norwegian lendir menn / Skjoldung-Yngling aristocracy; threw his high-seat pillars into the Atlantic to settle Reykjavik ('Smoky Bay') in 874 CE.

nodes.name: Ketil Flatnose → Aud / Unn the Deep-Minded (Matriarch of Iceland) & Helgi the Lean
nodes.role: Christian Hebridean-Norse Matriarch of Western Iceland
sources: Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok, Ellwood 1898)
nodes.notes: Daughter of Norwegian ruler Ketil Flatnose of the Hebrides and widow of Olaf the White of Dublin; independently commanded a knarr vessel to claim Breidafjordur, becoming ancestress of major Icelandic clans and of Sturla Thordarson / Snorri Sturluson.

nodes.name: Thorvald Asvaldsson → Erik the Red (Greenland, 985 CE) → Leif Erikson (Vinland / North America, c. 1000 CE)
nodes.role: Norse Explorers Reaching Greenland & North America (Transatlantic Pre-Columbian Bridge)
sources: Book of the Settlement of Iceland (Landnamabok)
Vinland Sagas
nodes.notes: Icelandic lineage in Landnamabok bridging Europe across Greenland to Vinland (L'Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland) five centuries before 1492; sister Gudrid Thorbjarnardottir bore Snorri Thorfinnsson in Vinland!

nodes.name: Cunedda Wledig (Founder of Gwynedd) → Maelgwn Gwynedd → Cadwallon ap Cadfan → King Cadwaladr
nodes.era: c. 400–682 CE (J.E. Lloyd History of Wales Vol. 1)
nodes.role: Early Royal House of Gwynedd (Venedotia)
sources: Sir John Edward Lloyd A History of Wales (2nd ed. 1912 Vol. 1 pp.116–192)
nodes.notes: Migrated from Manaw Gododdin (Scotland) to North Wales to expel Irish settlers; descendants ruled Gwynedd through Maelgwn and Cadwallon to Cadwaladr Fendigaid.

nodes.name: Rhodri Mawr (Rhodri the Great, 844–878) → Anarawd & Cadell → Hywel Dda ('the Good', Codifier of Welsh Law)
nodes.era: 844–950 CE (Lloyd History of Wales Vol. 1 pp.323–356)
nodes.role: Unifiers & Lawgivers of Medieval Wales
sources: J.E. Lloyd A History of Wales Vol. 1 pp.323–356
nodes.notes: Rhodri Mawr united Gwynedd, Powys, and Seisyllwg; grandson Hywel Dda (c. 942) united nearly all Wales and codified the Cyfraith Hywel (Welsh Laws).

nodes.name: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn (Unifier of All Wales, 1055) → Owain Gwynedd → Llywelyn the Great → Llywelyn ap Gruffydd (d. 1282)
nodes.role: Sovereign Princes of Wales & Tudor Royal Ancestors
sources: J.E. Lloyd A History of Wales (1912)
nodes.notes: Culminated in Llywelyn ap Iorwerth (Llywelyn the Great) and Llywelyn ap Gruffydd ('the Last'), whose Anglesey/Gwynedd kinsmen Owen Tudor wed Queen Catherine of Valois -> English House of Tudor!

nodes.name: Keating's 12 Noble Tribes of the Gaels (Saorchlanna, Foras Feasa ar Eirinn): Leath Cuinn (Dal gCuinn, Dal Riada, Ui Neill) & Leath Mogha (Eber Finn → Eoghan Mor, Cormac Cas, Ceallachan of Cashel)
nodes.role: Master Gaelic Pedigrees Synchronizing Munster, Connacht, Ulster & Scotland
sources: Geoffrey Keating Foras Feasa ar Eirinn: Genealogies (Irish Texts Society 1902–1914)
nodes.notes: Provides full unbroken father-to-son Gaelic pedigrees for the 12 Saorchlanna (noble houses) under Milesian sons Eber Finn (Leath Mogha / Cashel / Dal gCais) and Eremon (Leath Cuinn / Dal Riada / Ui Neill), plus Ir and Ith.

nodes.name: Tughlugh Timur Khan (1st Muslim Khan of Moghulistan, 1347) → Khizr Khoja → Yunus Khan
nodes.role: Eastern Chagatai Khans of Kashgar, Turfan & Semirechye
sources: Mirza Muhammad Haidar Dughlat Tarikh-i-Rashidi (Ross & Elias 1895)
nodes.notes: Traces Eastern Moghulistan from Chagatai -> Duwa -> Esen Buqa -> Tughlugh Timur Khan (embraced Islam) -> Khizr Khoja -> Yunus Khan (maternal grandfather of Mughal Emperor Babur!).

nodes.name: Sultan Ahmad Alaq → Sultan Said Khan (Yarkand, 1514) & Mirza Muhammad Haidar Dughlat (Conqueror of Kashmir, 1540)
nodes.role: Dughlat Amir & Last Great Moghul Khans of Kashgaria & Kashmir
sources: Mirza Muhammad Haidar Dughlat Tarikh-i-Rashidi (1546)
nodes.notes: Sultan Said Khan (+ Dughlat general Mirza Haidar, cousin of Emperor Babur) campaigned across Ladakh, Baltistan, and Kashmir (where Haidar ruled 1540–1551 and authored Tarikh-i-Rashidi).

nodes.name: Skyid-lde Nyi-ma-mgon (Founder of Kingdom of Ladakh/Ngari, c. 900 CE) → Lhachen Palgyigon → Utpala
nodes.era: c. 900–1110 CE (La-dvags rGyal-rabs / Chronicles of Ladakh)
nodes.role: Tibetan Yarlung Prince Founding Western Tibetan Royal House
sources: A.H. Francke Antiquities of Indian Tibet Part II: Chronicles of Ladakh (1926 pp.71–100)
nodes.notes: Descendant of Tibetan Emperor Langdarma (Yarlung line traced to Okkaka/Śākya); migrated west c. 900 CE to divide Ngari among his three sons, with eldest Lhachen Palgyigon ruling Maryul/Ladakh.

nodes.name: King Bhagan (Namgyal Dynasty) → Jamyang Namgyal → King Sengge Namgyal ('Lion King' of Leh Palace, 1616–1642)
nodes.era: c. 1460–1642 CE (Chronicles of Ladakh Ch. VI–VIII)
nodes.role: Namgyal Kings of Ladakh & Builders of Nine-Story Leh Palace
sources: A.H. Francke Chronicles of Ladakh (1926 pp.101–135)
nodes.notes: Lha-chen Bhagan founded the Namgyal Dynasty; Jamyang Namgyal wed Balti princess Gyal Khatun, fathering great builder-king Sengge Namgyal (builder of Leh Palace & Hemis Monastery).

nodes.name: Sisodia / Guhila Rajputs of Mewar (Solar via Lava): Guhaditya → Bappa Rawal (734 CE) → Rana Kumbha → Rana Sanga → Maharana Pratap (1576)
nodes.role: Suryavamshi Solar House of Chittor & Udaipur
sources: James Tod Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1–2 (1829–1832)
nodes.notes: James Tod preserves the Udaipur/Mewar bardic chronicles tracing the Guhilot/Sisodia Ranas from Ayodhya's Rama -> Lava through Vallabhi -> Guhaditya -> Bappa Rawal (defended western India 734 CE) to Rana Kumbha, Rana Sanga, and Maharana Pratap.

nodes.name: Rathores of Marwar (Rao Siha → Rao Jodha of Jodhpur) & Kachwahas of Amber/Jaipur (Solar via Kusha: Raja Man Singh I → Sawai Jai Singh II)
nodes.era: 13th–18th c. CE (Tod Annals of Rajasthan Vol. 2)
nodes.role: Suryavamshi Rajput Houses of Jodhpur & Jaipur
sources: James Tod Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vol. 2
nodes.notes: Traces Marwar Rathores (Kannauj -> Rao Siha -> Rao Jodha, 1459) and Amber Kachwahas (Rama's son Kusha -> Gwalior/Amber -> Man Singh I -> astronomer-king Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur).

nodes.name: Prithviraj Chauhan of Ajmer & Delhi (1178–1192) & Bhati Yadavas of Jaisalmer (Rawal Jaisal, 1156)
nodes.era: 12th c. CE (Tod Annals of Rajasthan Vols. 1–2)
nodes.role: Agnikula Chauhan & Chandravamshi Yadava Rajputs
sources: James Tod Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan Vols. 1–2
nodes.notes: Chahamanas/Chauhans culminating in Prithviraj Chauhan III, alongside the Lunar Yadava Bhatis traced from Krishna/Dvaraka to Rawal Jaisal (founder of Jaisalmer, 1156 CE).

nodes.name: Harivamsha & Matsya Purana: Vaivasvata Manu's Flood Ship & Complete Yadava-Vrishni House (Ugrasena, Kamsa, Akrura, Pradyumna, Aniruddha & Samba)
nodes.era: Vedic / Puranic Canon (Harivamsha; Matsya Purana I–X)
nodes.role: Supplement to Mahabharata & Great Flood Purana
sources: Harivamsha English Prose Trans. (M.N. Dutt 1897)
Matsya Purana (SBH 17, Taluqdar of Oudh 1916)
nodes.notes: Detailed account of Vaivasvata Manu's seven-rishis ark tied to Mt. Himavan during the Great Flood (Matsya Purana I–II) and complete Vrishni/Andhaka/Yadava clan lineages around Krishna (Harivamsha).

nodes.name: Dionysius of Halicarnassus (Roman Antiquities I): Arcadian Evander of Pallantium, Aeneas + Lavinia, Silvius → Numitor, Amulius & Rhea Silvia
nodes.role: Complete Alba Longa King List Linking Troy & Arcadia to Rome
sources: Dionysius of Halicarnassus Roman Antiquities Book I (Loeb)
nodes.notes: Connects early Italy to Greece via Arcadian Evander (founder of Pallantium on the Palatine Hill) and traces the 15 Silvian kings of Alba Longa down to Numitor, vestal Rhea Silvia, and twins Romulus & Remus.

nodes.name: Pausanias (Description of Greece) & H.F. Clinton (Fasti Hellenici Vols. 1 & 3): Pelasgus, Arcas, Aegialeus, Codrus of Athens & Olympiad Chronology
nodes.role: Regional Greek Founding Genealogies & Synchronized Classical Annals
sources: Pausanias Description of Greece
H.F. Clinton Fasti Hellenici Vols. 1 & 3 (1830–1834)
nodes.notes: Pausanias preserves local genealogies for Attica, Sicyon (Aegialeus), Arcadia (Pelasgus -> Lycaon -> Arcas), and Messenia, synchronized year-by-year with Biblical/Persian history in Clinton's Fasti Hellenici.

nodes.name: Kojiki (Chamberlain 1932): Ame-no-Minakanushi → Izanagi & Izanami → Susanoo (→ Okuninushi) & Ninigi (+ Konohanasakuya-hime) → Yamato Takeru & Nintoku
nodes.role: Earliest Complete Japanese Imperial & Izumo Kami Genealogy
sources: Basil Hall Chamberlain Translation of Ko-ji-ki (2nd ed. 1932)
nodes.notes: Chamberlain's annotated Kojiki preserves every kami of the Age of the Gods, the Izumo line of Susanoo & Okuninushi, Ninigi's descent to Hyuga, Prince Yamato Takeru, and Emperor Nintoku.

nodes.name: Hulbert's History of Korea (Vols. 1–2): Goguryeo (Gwanggaeto the Great), Baekje (King Onjo), Kaya (Kim Suro) & Silla (Queen Seondeok & Kim Yu-sin)
nodes.role: Unified Synthesis of Ancient Korean Three Kingdoms & Later Silla
sources: Homer B. Hulbert The History of Korea Vols. 1–2 (1905)
nodes.notes: Synchronizes Goguryeo (Jumong -> Gwanggaeto), Baekje (Onjo), Gaya (Suro), and Silla (Queen Seondeok, General Kim Yu-sin & King Muyeol unifying the peninsula in 668 CE).
